editorial.marketOverview: US equities are closed Saturday. Friday November 20 Nasdaq Composite -5.28% (Reuters), SOX about -11% (Reuters), Nasdaq 100 -5.6% (FT) and QQQ -5.67% (secondary closing report) depict an unusually sharp technology-led liquidation. Barron's reported Friday VIX close 37.66. Nasdaq 100 was down 10.4% for the week according to FT. These are Friday observations with differing publication times, not synchronized Saturday quotes.
editorial.whatChanged: Compared with the 04:46 EST snapshot, newly reviewed November 21 weekend reporting and TD Economics/Newsquawk next-week calendars corroborate already known Friday losses and Monday-Wednesday catalysts. The curated Open Watch file still contains 174 events, unchanged since 2026-11-21T00:44:37+00:00. No verified new event or price observation materially changes the expected three-day trajectory.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Semiconductor underperformance, negative breadth and extreme Friday volatility maintain a bearish near-term regime, even though a sharp oversold bounce is plausible. Friday's 10Y yield near 4.93% was reported by Reuters but lacks a synchronized 2Y; the earlier 4.94% versus 4.65% implies +29 bp only for the older indicative pair. Direct FedWatch, VXN and same-contract-maturity Brent/WTI are unverified. Fed expectations may be hawkish, but no fresh exact probabilities are asserted. No single headline is treated as a proven cause of Friday's market decline.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23: high volatility and downside continuation risk versus a potentially powerful short-covering rebound; US flash PMIs at 09:45 ET can change yields and tech sentiment. Tuesday November 24: consumer confidence at 10:00 ET and Analog Devices/Dell earnings test consumer and AI-hardware sentiment. Wednesday November 25: 08:30 ET GDP, income/spending and durable-goods releases plus 14:00 ET Beige Book concentrate event risk ahead of Thanksgiving. All are expected catalysts with unknown outcomes, not observed responses.
editorial.bullCase: Oversold positioning and elevated hedging demand could produce a sharp relief rally. A durable turn requires QQQ and SOX/SMH strengthening together, broadening advancers and retreating VIX/VXN, ideally accompanied by falling synchronized Treasury yields.
editorial.bearCase: Friday's extreme chip losses and Nasdaq 100 bear-market drawdown may lead investors to sell rallies. Further AI capital-spending doubts, hawkish repricing or disappointing hardware guidance would amplify weakness, but remain conditional scenarios rather than known future events.
